_comment: The application commit this workflow is approved to deploy.
A 40-hex app_sha input establishes SYNTAX, not approval. Every commit on
every branch is 40 hex characters. This file is the approval, it lives on
the default branch, and changing it is a reviewed change.
The candidate checkout never supplies its own approval: this file is read
from the operational checkout (the commit the workflow itself ran from),
never from the application commit under deployment.
Future acceptances are a one-line edit here, reviewed like any other.
packageLabel: The whole expo package: kiosk link control, station enrolment, the CORRECTED combined movement goal (no silent backfill, one active parent per child), the queue that calls a participant by the name they chose, the phone-or-queue journey after activity selection, the reworked follow-along player, and the Manage sheet creative pass.
_expectedPriorFunctionsNote: 31 before, 40 after. The prior count was established by run 35420931701 reading the live project. This candidate adds NINE: wsfCreateCombinedGoal, wsfCombinedGoalPulse, wsfCloseCombinedGoal, wsfJoinQueue, wsfLeaveQueue, wsfMyQueueEntry, wsfQueueState, wsfCallNext and wsfFinishServing. EXPECT THE FIRST RUN TO FAIL: nine new services means nine invoker-policy sets and this project’s deploy service account cannot perform them, exactly as run 35420410645 failed on seven. The services persist, so a SECOND run updates rather than creates and completes. That is a description of what this project does, not an endorsement: functions created that way are NOT callable, and a green second run must never be reported as a working capability. The seven station services remain invoker_iam_check_enabled and the hosted smoke now probes the four public ones so the gap fails loudly. wsfGoalPulse keeps its nine-field contract, asserted again by 423 callable tests with a combined goal and a queue running.
